segments.line: Seven AM. Your alarm goes off. You
roll out of bed, and your
pajama pants slide straight down to your ankles.
In the bathroom mirror, the zit on your chin is gone.
So is the scar on your knee from the bike crash last summer. You
grab your phone. Face ID doesn't recognize you. Three tries.
Enter passcode.
At breakfast, you say good morning, and your voice
cracks. Upward.
Your little sister Ellie spits out her cereal.
Mo texts you. Bus in five. You
run outside, and your
sneakers are half a size too big.
Your mom checks your height against the pencil marks on the kitchen door frame.
You're not at last night's mark. You're at the mark from exactly one year ago.
Yesterday you were fifteen. Today you're fourteen.
And tonight, at midnight, it happens again.
What if you aged backwards, and couldn't stop?
At first, it sounds like a superpower.
But every clock counts down to something.
And yours just started.
